Difference from a decoder: A multiplexer has multiple data inputs and one output (many-to-one), selected by select lines; a decoder has one (or few) inputs and multiple outputs (one-to-many), activating exactly one output line based on the input code.

text:
Prove the Boolean expression using Boolean laws. Also, mention the law used at each step:
F = (x' + z) + [ (y' + z) . (x' + y) ]' = 1

Let T = (y'+z).(x'+y).
Step 1: T' = (y'+z)' + (x'+y)'   [De Morgan's law]
        = (y.z') + (x.y')      [De Morgan's law again]
Step 2: F = x' + z + y.z' + x.y'
Step 3: Group x' + x.y' = x' + y'   [Absorption: A' + A.B = A' + B]
Step 4: F = x' + y' + z + y.z'
Step 5: y' + y.z' = y' + z'          [Absorption: A' + A.B = A' + B]
Step 6: F = x' + (y' + z') ... rearranged: F = x' + y' + z + z' 
Step 7: z + z' = 1   [Complement law]
Step 8: F = x' + y' + 1 = 1   [X + 1 = 1]
keyPoints: De Morgan's law breaks the bracket into two AND terms
Absorption law: A' + A.B = A' + B, used twice
Complement law: z + z' = 1
Identity law: anything + 1 = 1, so F = 1
